_schema: The end of the scrub, and the one station that is not a place he painted. It has the shape station 7 had at M6 -- no canvases, a share of tau declared in seconds -- and M8 adds the fields it needs: `ground.bare`, which keeps the cloth under it the primed canvas of station 0 however far tau has gone, `pacing.nothing`, which is how long it holds before the crows come, and `crows.after`, which says that its crows are the ones that come rather than the ones that have been at the edge of the frame since Arles. After M9 adds `coda`: the painting the walk ends on, which stands past the end of the road rather than in the station, so it is not one of this station's canvases and has no share of tau.
title: After
_canvases: None. DESIGN 7: nothing, held far too long, then the crows again, and the end. The coda is BUILD M8's decision -- nothing, or the canvases in their museums -- and this file is the first of the two, which is DESIGN 15's current position.
_ground: Bare primed canvas, lit, with nothing on it and no charcoal line across it: the loading screen with its one mark taken away. It stands six hundred metres out of the back of the last field, so the field is behind you and in the dark.
_pacing: beat is how many seconds of tau this station is, and it is half a second because there is nothing here to scrub through: the end of the scrub is a place, not a stretch. nothing is how long it holds before the crows come, in the viewer's own seconds rather than tau's, because tau has run out. Twenty-four is DESIGN 7's 'far too long' made into a number to be argued with, and M8's testers are what argue with it. Autoplay never arrives here -- it stops at the last stroke of the field -- so the only way in is a hand.
_crows: Nine, off Wheatfield with Crows, and the first time any of them is in plain view: they come in from behind, over the viewer's head, and circle in front over the bare canvas, which is where they stay. DESIGN 7's diagram puts 'bare primed canvas, and the crows' at the top of the piece, and this is it.
_coda: On the author's word, after M9: the walk ends on his portrait. DESIGN 15 left the coda open between nothing and the canvases in their museums, and M8 built the nothing; the author's answer is the painter. Self-Portrait as a Painter is the last canvas he painted in Paris before he left for Arles, and the last in the corridor at station 2. It is hung again here from the same stroke record, not in this station but past the end of the road: `beyond` metres out from where the walk on its own stops, on the easel every station has, grown to hold a canvas `height` metres tall. None of it is there until you are on this bare canvas. Then the easel paints itself in, the canvas comes up primed and is held for `hold` seconds, which is what is left of the nothing, and he paints himself on it in `paint` seconds. All of it keeps that time from where it begins and runs `approach` times as fast at its foot, so that walking up to it brings him out on the canvas as you come: on the author's word, so that it is not waited for. The walk on its own stops where the road does, with the whole canvas in view; the last eighty metres are a hand's. The nine crows of this station circled it at first, from the height of his hands to over its top; on the author's word they are gone, an omen over him and not a tribute, and the sky past the last field is empty. It keeps a haze of its own, an eighth of the station's, so that his colour carries the eighty metres.
